Thr254Met substitution sits in the beta strand of the CD40L TNF homology domain at a trimer or CD40-contact face, and the bulkier Met side chain disrupts homotrimer packing and CD40 engagement, so the mutant subunit cannot form or hold a functional trimer and CD40 binding and signalling are lost.","supports":["E2","E3","E4","E9","E11","E12","E14","E18","E10"],"would_refute":"Thr254 side-chain atoms in the CD40-CD40L complex (3QD6) and in the trimer built from the AlphaFold model lie more than about 8 Å from any atom of the partner chain, and modelling Met at 254 leaves the trimer contact area and the CD40 interface unchanged within about 5%.","latest_verdict":"unchanged","label":"agent-generated hypothesis"},{"id":"H2","mechanism_class":"stability_folding","starting_rank":2,"statement":"Thr254Met is a buried or strand-core substitution in the CD40L TNF homology domain that adds steric bulk and loses the Thr hydroxyl, so the beta-sandwich folds less stably, the protein is partly misfolded or degraded, and secretion and trimer assembly fall below the level needed for CD40 signalling.","supports":["E3","E4","E5","E6","E7","E8","E15","E9"],"would_refute":"In the AlphaFold model and in the 8 experimental structures, residue 254 has relative solvent accessibility above 50% change.","latest_verdict":"supported","label":"agent-generated hypothesis"}],"results":[{"test_id":"T1","test_kind":"stability_effect","summary":"FoldX predicts a folding ΔΔG of +2.74 kcal/mol for
